wintercity_e03_entry.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_entry.text: Day 829 began with wages rather than a new promise. Lan placed the completed receiving records beside a shallow tray of copper. The first appointment had covered six four-hour mornings from Day 817 through Day 822; the half-hour orientation absence reduced its payment by one copper at the agreed two-copper hourly rate. The total was forty-seven. The separate five mornings from Day 824 through Day 828 had all been completed, giving forty more. Yue counted eighty-seven copper and signed for that payment.

wintercity_e03_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_002.text: Lan kept the work copies; Yue kept the signed wage receipt. The correction of the accepted valve-seat subtotal appeared in both. No later factory offer would turn those completed hours into a debt, and refusing such an offer could not erase the paid receipt. The temporary extensions had now ended. Lan had another finite need beginning tomorrow: a ten-morning stock comparison through Day 839. Its tasks excluded heavy lifting and apparatus operation. Yue asked for the proposed hours before accepting.

wintercity_e03_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_003.text: The new appointment offered four hours a morning at the same two-copper hourly rate, with no guaranteed work afterward. It would pay eighty copper after ten completed mornings, less any agreed absence. Yue read the ordinary termination procedure and the payment obligation for hours already done. She accepted, reserving the afternoon of Day 830 for any existing appointment and her own arrival tasks. The third contract was a separate decision about ordinary work, not a hidden renewal of any incoming mine post.

wintercity_e03_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_004.text: Before the payment tray was cleared, Yue put thirty-two copper into a cloth purse marked for later travel. The remaining fifty-five went into her current-city account. The reserve was ordinary earned money, not fuel or practice capacity. It could be used if immediate necessities required, but doing so would reduce what remained for departure. She did not call it untouchable in a way that would make a future hungry evening disappear. She wanted an exit fund whose actual contents she could count.

wintercity_e03_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_005.text: She paid the next due meal charge at her lodging and recorded it with the lodging arrangement's own terms. A staff bed, a courtyard room, and an independent inn had different schedules; none gave unlimited meals. She left the confidential mine cover closed until she needed its authorized purpose. There were arrival permissions to finish before they expired, but no mine wages waiting in the winter city. What had been completed and paid at the mine remained completed and paid.

wintercity_e03_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_006.text: Lan sent her to the fuel yard after lunch to learn the stock categories she would compare on the new appointment. The lesson was observation, not permission to release charge. The yard's ordinary charcoal stood under a shed, while compatible apparatus cylinders occupied locked racks on the dry side. Empty returns had their own area. Yue could not add all three counts into one useful-supply total. A container's presence told her little until its owner, content, and permitted use were identified.

wintercity_e03_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_007.text: The charcoal sacks were sold by accepted weight and dryness class. A cylinder was received by seal, calibration record, and weighed contents, with a return requirement for its housing. A private apparatus might accept only one compatible cylinder class. Lan showed Yue a pair of cylinders with similar colours and different connector marks. The wrong class could fit after someone filed a pin, which was why filing the pin was prohibited. Physical fit was an insufficient argument about safe use.

wintercity_e03_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_008.text: At the scale, a worker named Hu Yan opened the witness-weight box with the yard clerk. Yan held a current municipal apparatus licence and a separate qualification for the public training rig. She did not claim a cultivation realm from that licence. Yue could recognize competence established for a named job without inventing spiritual capacity. Yan invited her to watch a calibration cycle from behind the marked rail. The cycle discharged a measured quantity into an inspected wick, which darkened as it was used.

wintercity_e03_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_009.text: The calibration discharge belonged in the source account. It did not become unexplained leakage or a free preliminary step. Yue watched the yard clerk subtract it before calculating usable stock. Her personal reserve stayed out of that account. Yan asked her to say where a later half-unit practice input would be entered. Yue pointed to the operator's separate task sheet. The sheet would distinguish the practitioner's expenditure from the external supply doing the apparatus's larger work.

wintercity_e03_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_010.text: A delivery cart rolled in with two full cylinders and one returned empty housing. Yue counted the physical objects, then watched the clerk enter their contents separately. The returned housing could not count as a third fuel delivery. Its seller would credit the deposit after inspecting the fittings. The carrier asked whether the credit was immediate. The clerk showed the inspection deadline and a receipt proving the housing had been returned today. These duties mattered because a carrier could not pay for indefinite custody with goodwill.

wintercity_e03_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_011.text: On the far side of the yard, a charcoal barrow's wheel slipped into a shallow drain channel. The barrow tilted, and the worker pushing it let go rather than try to catch the full load. A sack split against the paving. People stepped back from the loose charcoal. Yan used the ordinary yard brake to stop the next barrow entering the lane while two store workers secured the first. Yue stayed outside the marked space and held the new arrivals at its entrance.

wintercity_e03_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_012.text: The incident delayed three deliveries. One of the store workers fetched a long-handled scoop; another checked the axle. The spilled charcoal could be recovered only into a separate sack for reinspection, because paving grit had mixed with it. No cultivator waved a hand and restored accepted stock. Yue copied the incident time and the affected delivery references. The barrow worker's release had prevented his arm from taking the whole falling load. It had still cost material, time, and a repair.

wintercity_e03_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_013.text: Yan reopened the lane after the damaged barrow had been moved and the drain cleared. She asked the worker about his wrist. He said it hurt when he twisted the handle. She sent him to the ordinary clinic attendant instead of asking him to finish the route first. The yard supervisor arranged another worker's coverage and recorded the interruption. Yue saw practical care and accountability happen in the same hour. Neither required the injured person to make himself useful before being examined.

wintercity_e03_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_014.text: The clinic's temporary yard room contained clean water, splints, and a low examination chair. Its attendant, Zhou An, checked the worker's wrist and asked what movement caused pain. She did not call the absence of a visible break proof that he could carry again. He left with an ordinary support and restrictions for a follow-up check. The supervisor could schedule him around those restrictions or give him the stated recovery leave. Calling the injury minor would not erase either option's cost.

wintercity_e03_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_015.text: Zhou An told Yue where the full clinic stood and which hours handled urgent work injuries. She spoke to Yue as another worker, not as a promised future patient. The clinic used an agreed fee schedule and had a dispute route for unpaid employment coverage. Ordinary visitors could pay for ordinary care. A contested employer charge would be handled after immediate examination where the urgent policy applied. Yue copied the address because an accident could occur before the person hurt had settled a legal argument.

wintercity_e03_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_016.text: Yan checked the public training rig after the calibration lesson. Its table had a mechanical stop, an ordinary isolation lever, and a marked grounded release. A padded runout space stood beside it, not overhead. The operator could step back rather than stand trapped between the moving arm and a wall. Yue asked why the pads were placed where they were. Yan described an earlier ordinary slip during a harmless low-load demonstration. Preparing for that possibility did not predict which future visitor would fall.

wintercity_e03_017.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_017.text: The rig's rule required an independent observer for any comparative load demonstration. The observer would verify input limits and call the stop. The operator still retained responsibility to release at her own warning signs. No observer could make an excessive throughput safe by watching it carefully. Yue read that sentence twice. She would later have to decide whether to participate in a comparison; if she did, the consent would include the apparatus, the conditions, and the real possibility that she would simply lose.

wintercity_e03_018.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_018.text: Yan demonstrated the ordinary isolation with the rig uncharged. Yue practised locating the handle with her eyes closed, then opened them before touching anything. She was allowed the uncharged orientation, not a powered trial. A worker beside them arranged the runout pad and checked that the rear passage stayed clear. These actions would matter if a later public comparison became crowded. The rule against spectators entering that passage was already part of the posted demonstration procedure, not a favour added for a particular contestant.

wintercity_e03_019.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_019.text: In the evening, Yue's actual lodging arrangement determined which door she used and which heat hours applied. She read its current end date again. The receiving extension could qualify a staff resident for more annex nights, but it did not automatically renew a paid room. A courtyard occupant had to pay the next share before voting on future hours. An inn guest needed the next meal and room receipts. Whatever she chose, the next commitment still had to be made in its own terms.

wintercity_e03_020.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_020.text: The Day 830 morning shift began with cylinder housings. Yue compared return receipts with the empty-rack tally. Two credited housings remained on the rack awaiting collection; one newly returned housing had not yet passed inspection. The tally described physical custody, while the credit ledger described completed acceptance. They could show different totals without contradiction. Yue wrote the distinction at the top of her working page so someone reading quickly would not announce a fuel shortage from an empty-housing count.

wintercity_e03_021.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_021.text: After work she followed the actual incoming permission shown on her arrival receipt. A public-source registration, a timed private comparison seat, or independent observations carried different afternoon tasks. An old traveller with a partly illegible receipt would still be able to finish ordinary arrival work; missing records would not give her a private appointment or make her a worker delegate. Yue took the relevant cover to its proper desk and asked that the reply use the same limits as the registered permission.

wintercity_e03_022.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_022.text: When the incoming afternoon had been handled, Yue stopped at a food stall beside the baths. Its owner sold a small bowl of noodles at one price and a larger bowl at another. She bought the larger bowl because she had eaten little since morning. A girl at the counter was learning to add the day's sales. She counted the bowl as two small ones until her father corrected the different price. Yue waited while the girl changed her slate and returned the right change.

wintercity_e03_023.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_023.text: The girl asked whether Yue was a powerful cultivator. Yue said she could perform certain measured small tasks and still needed noodles. The girl laughed, uncertain whether that was an answer. Her father asked Yue not to make cultivation promises to the child. She agreed. The child's interest did not require a demonstration, and Yue had no inspected practice space beside a cooking pot. She pointed instead to the girl's corrected sum, which would help the stall sooner than a spark.

wintercity_e03_024.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_024.text: A cold gust came down the stair street while she ate. The vendor drew a canvas screen across the exposed side, leaving the stove's ventilation clear. Customers moved their stools. Yue helped hold the screen until he tied it, keeping her hands away from the hot frame. The practical adjustment made the meal more comfortable without consuming a cylinder from the heat yard. Borrowed winter could describe the city's trade, but ordinary shelter still did some of its most immediate work.

wintercity_e03_025.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_025.text: At the information room, an announcement invited public clients to the closure-calendar meeting on Day 838. Yue put it beside the lodging receipt rather than beside her practice application. Speaking at the meeting would concern the actual service she used and the authority she held. Her knowledge of a training rig did not give her a vote over a courtyard. Ning confirmed that written questions could be submitted before the meeting, with the submitter's name disclosed only under the published rule.

wintercity_e03_026.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_026.text: A tenant standing nearby wanted to bring the raw medical history of an elderly neighbour to prove that a closure would be harmful. Ning explained the separate consent requirement again. The tenant could describe the general need for accessible warm hours and ask what service was planned. The neighbour's private history would need the neighbour's own decision about disclosure. Yue watched the tenant revise her request. More detailed evidence could be more intrusive without being necessary to the first practical question.

wintercity_e03_027.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_027.text: On Day 831, Lan assigned Yue the cylinder withdrawal account. She would compare authorized requests and completed issues, not approve new uses herself. Yan demonstrated the three-copy form. One stayed at the rack, one travelled with the cylinder, and one returned after the task with residual content and housing condition recorded. Yue checked the serial marks before copying. A cylinder that changed hands without its form could leave both stock and responsibility uncertain even if the immediate task succeeded.

wintercity_e03_028.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_028.text: The first issue went to an inspected bath apparatus. It requested a particular class for a limited public washing interval. The bath operator checked the connector, the seal, and the usable content before signing custody. No one treated the operator's signature as a surrender of their right to reject a damaged cylinder. Yue entered the completed issue only after the cylinder had actually left the rack. A request alone would not reduce physical stock, although it reserved a quantity under the yard's rules.

wintercity_e03_029.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_029.text: The second request lacked an observer's current signature. The supervisor held it rather than ask Yue to fill the blank. Its applicant came to the counter, annoyed by the delay. Yan showed the date on the old qualification. The applicant arranged an appropriately qualified observer and returned before the reserved quantity expired. The task proceeded later that day. A hold could impose a real inconvenience without secretly being a permanent ban, and a corrected document could remove a hold without changing the apparatus's physical limits.

wintercity_e03_030.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_030.text: A client at the next counter wanted two cylinders for a heater inspected for one. The yard refused the issue because the increased supply was not part of its approved procedure. The client offered more money. The answer remained no until the changed arrangement had been reviewed. Yue saw a limit that commerce could not simply lift. Payment could cover a new inspection or a larger qualified installation; it could not make an unexamined connection safe merely because the buyer was willing.

wintercity_e03_031.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_031.text: Yue's own public training application remained incomplete. She had an established input ceiling and an observed shutdown arrangement, but she still needed to select a permitted task and its independent observer. Yan suggested using the lowest useful load if she applied. Yue wrote that suggestion without treating it as an approval. The useful quarter-unit result of earlier tasks could not be assumed for this city's different instrument. Even a familiar nominal input would need an actual measured application.

wintercity_e03_032.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_032.text: At noon, a returned bath cylinder had more residual content than predicted. The operator had closed the washing interval early because the hot-water pipe required inspection. The return sheet recorded actual duration, useful work, and residual measurement. Unused supply did not count as stolen warmth, nor did it prove the original estimate fraudulent. Yue asked the supervisor to check the calibration and the shortened schedule before reconciling the account. The predicted figure could be amended only after identifying why reality differed.

wintercity_e03_033.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_033.text: The operator's clients received the replacement arrangement stated in the bath terms: a later washing interval at the same paid class, or a refund for those unable to attend. Some chose each. Their choices changed the bath's cash and future bookings. Yue did not count both refunds and replacement places as delivered to everyone. The returned cylinder's residual charge stayed in the yard's account after inspection, available only for another authorized task. One interrupted service had produced several different unfinished matters.

wintercity_e03_034.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_034.text: That afternoon she walked past the works' main gate. A notice announced a public demonstration by Gao Shen during the cold festival preparation, with comparative apparatus trials subject to municipal approval. It advertised reliable power but did not list every condition. Yue copied the public date and looked for the approval reference. She found it on the lower board, where the demonstration's output limits and observer requirements were posted. The owner's spiritual capacity was real; the audience would still need a safe place to stand.

wintercity_e03_035.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_035.text: Yan was named as one apparatus operator for the event, and an independent municipal examiner would supervise the approved comparative station. Zhou An's clinic would provide a paid ordinary first-aid attendant during the specified hours. The runout passage and isolation points were drawn on the plan. Yue recognized the arrangement she had seen earlier. If she later chose to compare her own capacity, those preparations would already exist. They would not guarantee that her body could tolerate every permitted attempt.

wintercity_e03_036.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_036.text: The plan also stated that a participant could withdraw before the comparison began or release during it. Withdrawal would leave the comparative result unearned. It would not cancel wages from unrelated completed work. Yue noticed the clause because a public crowd could make a sensible retreat feel like disgrace. The rule gave retreat a practical form; it could not force a frightened person to use it. She would have to remember that distinction if pride ever made a clear handle seem distant.

wintercity_e03_037.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_037.text: Rui Wen invited Yue to a repair supper on Day 832. The umbrella workers were pooling inexpensive food after an afternoon of patching frames. Yue offered vegetables rather than money she had not agreed to contribute. The supper was not a hearing, and no one asked for a cultivation certificate. They would use a room purchased for those hours. When the room closed, the guests would go home or find another lawful place, without extending the workers' allocation through applause.

wintercity_e03_038.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_038.text: On the cold term's first morning, Day 832, the street flags changed in sequence. The inspected main opened by sections while return temperatures were checked. There was no single brilliant instant when the city became warm. Some rooms were already heated by their own stoves; others waited for their agreed main interval. Yue watched a keeper leave a closed sign up until the section's indicator settled. His restraint disappointed the queue but avoided promising service before it could actually be delivered.

wintercity_e03_039.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_039.text: At the yard, stock issues increased. Yue worked through the forms in order of authorized collection time rather than the loudest client's voice. Lan handled priority disputes under the posted procedure. A clinic request and a private workshop request had different priority classes, but both still required compatible supply and actual stock. Priority could move a claimant forward in the queue; it could not produce an absent cylinder. Yue recorded a partial issue where the clinic's approved alternative used less supply for fewer rooms.

wintercity_e03_040.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_040.text: The clinic did not pretend that the partial issue warmed every corridor. It kept the examination rooms at their planned interval and moved waiting chairs into one served area, within its safe capacity. Patients unable to fit there received the specified alternative waiting place. Zhou An later told Yue the arrangement was awkward and workable for the day. The report preserved both facts. Calling it a success should not hide the reduced service; calling it a failure should not erase the people actually kept warm.

wintercity_e03_041.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_041.text: A cylinder arrived with a readable seal and an unreadable calibration date. Yue held it for confirmation. The carrier said the seller would be furious over another delay. Lan took responsibility for applying the receiving rule. The seller's office produced a legible duplicate, and the inspection went ahead. Yue was grateful that the job's division put an employer behind its worker's correct hold. A rule could be sound and still useless if every practical penalty fell on the person asked to enforce it.

wintercity_e03_042.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_042.text: At the repair supper, Wen's apprentice burned one piece of flatbread and scraped the black edge into the waste dish. Nobody asked Yue to draw the burnt taste out with qi. She ate the remaining bread with vegetables and listened to a story about an umbrella returned with the wrong handle. The owner had preferred the wrong handle after trying it, so the workers had documented the substitution rather than insist on restoring a more elegant order that no one wanted.

wintercity_e03_043.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_043.text: Jia arrived late with leftover beans from her shorter route. She had sold fewer jars but returned with less spoilage than the week before. The account mattered to her, not as a victory over somebody else's business plan. Yue asked whether the change left enough for her rent. Jia said this week it did; next week remained a question. Their table held an ordinary future, with uncertainty and food in the same bowl, instead of a speech proving that every sensible choice would prosper.

wintercity_e03_044.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_044.text: When the purchased room hours ended, the workers put out the ordinary stove and checked the window latches. Yue helped collect dishes. The key holder examined the room before returning the deposit receipt. It was a closure they had prepared while they were still enjoying the evening. No one lost the value of the supper because it ended. Walking home in cold air, Yue felt the pleasure of having spent an evening among people who did not require her to resolve the city.

wintercity_e03_045.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_045.text: On Day 833, the yard account showed a short residual return from a workshop task. Yue did not accuse the operator. Yan compared the task duration, calibration discharge, measured output, and known housing loss. Those explained part of the difference. The remaining discrepancy required the workshop's own observation sheet. Yue sent a precise request rather than fill the gap with her favourite theory. A good account could establish where information was missing without turning that absence into a convenient villain.

wintercity_e03_046.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_046.text: The workshop replied that its permitted test had been interrupted and restarted once. The restart used a documented clearing discharge omitted from the initial return form. Yan verified the local record and amended the account. The missing quantity was now explained as actual spent charge, not recovered fuel. The corrected form did not refill the cylinder. Yue noted the restart cost on the general comparison sheet so a future estimate would not assume that every interrupted task could begin again for free.

wintercity_e03_047.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_047.text: At the same desk, an applicant asked to copy the corrected workshop procedure. The record's public portion described the account correction; the detailed method remained owned by the workshop. Lan gave the applicant the public summary and the proper route for requesting the rest. Yue recognized the boundary from the incoming mine materials. A city could improve collective understanding without declaring every useful invention common property. Consent was part of practical knowledge because other people could otherwise stop trusting its circulation.

wintercity_e03_048.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_048.text: In the afternoon, Yue visited the public training rig again with her proposed task form. Yan read the input ceiling and asked how Yue intended to stop after a false indicator. Yue described the ordinary isolation and grounded release, then pointed to the space where she would step back. She did not yet book the powered task. The form still needed the independent observer's agreement and the selected fuel source. Preparing those details could save trouble; it could not stand in for the test itself.

wintercity_e03_049.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_049.text: Yan showed her the operator qualification register. Names were tied to apparatus classes and expiration dates. Gao Shen's broad spiritual capacity did not automatically put him on every apparatus list, though the works employed people qualified for its own installations. Yue's narrower capacity would not excuse an unqualified task either. The same demand for a named relevant competence applied to both, while their actual abilities remained unequal. A fair procedure did not require the physically weaker person to win.

wintercity_e03_050.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_050.text: The independent examiner for the festival station was named Luo Pei. Her municipal registration included load comparisons on the specific rig and emergency isolation for its external supply. Yue read the public record instead of guessing from the examiner's age or robe. Luo Pei would judge the result, and Yan would handle the instrument. Zhou An's attendant would handle ordinary injury care. The divided roles made each person's task clearer; they did not create a magical promise that no contestant could leave hurt or disappointed.

wintercity_e03_051.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_051.text: After the Day 833 shift, Yue found the street market crowded beneath patched awnings. A seller had arranged small wooden birds beside packets of ordinary seed. She chose neither, stopping to watch a child repair a bird's paper tail with paste. The child wanted the tail longer than the seller's example. The seller warned that a longer tail would make it harder to balance on the finger. They tried both lengths. The child preferred the awkward longer one and paid the same price.

wintercity_e03_052.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_052.text: At the vegetable stall, a woman named Du Ling removed one glove to handle change. The skin at her knuckles was cracked. Yue did not ask what illness she had or suggest that cultivation could mend it.

wintercity_e03_053.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_053.text: Ling said the glove made small coins difficult and asked Yue to hold the purchase bag open. They finished that ordinary task together. Ling ran a washhouse and was considering shorter winter hours because cold hands made the work slower. She would decide after speaking with her assistants. She invited Yue to ask about the public hours at the washhouse counter another day, where a staff member could confirm them from the current notice.

wintercity_e03_054.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_054.text: A gust lifted the corner of an awning while they talked. The stallholder lowered its exposed side and moved two baskets inward. Ling took her vegetables; Yue bought a small turnip. Their conversation ended because the seller needed space to secure his stock, not because one of them had discovered a decisive answer. Yue later remembered Ling's name when reading the washhouse service list. She had met an owner whose own body and employees' schedules would shape what a printed allocation could accomplish.

wintercity_e03_055.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_055.text: Near the square, the music student from the inn tested a repaired bow under the lee of a wall. He had chosen the shorter room contract and now needed a different rehearsal place for one evening. A public room allowed quiet practice only during a particular interval, so he waited until it began. He asked Yue whether the phrase sounded hurried. She said which notes she could distinguish and admitted that she knew no trained standard. He wanted a listener, not a flattering expert.

wintercity_e03_056.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_056.text: When his permitted interval ended, he packed the bow despite still wanting another attempt. Yue accompanied him to the bread stall. His audition remained uncertain, and he had paid for a room arrangement that left him able to travel. He could regret its higher daily cost on an ordinary cold evening without pretending the longer commitment had disappeared. They ate outside because the stall's sheltered seats were full. The bread warmed their hands briefly; afterward they put their gloves back on.

wintercity_e03_057.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_057.text: On the walk home, Yue heard a bird strike the sheltered window of a closed shop. It fell onto the shallow sill, stunned. The shopkeeper came out, kept passers-by back, and watched it from a distance rather than seize it for a portent. After several minutes it moved into a crouch, then flew unevenly to a nearby hedge. The shopkeeper would hang a visible strip inside the glass tomorrow. Yue stayed only until the pavement was clear, leaving the bird's next movements to the bird.

wintercity_e03_058.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_058.text: On Day 834, wind carried fine ash from an upper workshop into the yard. Lan closed the exposed paper table until the workshop's vent problem had been addressed. Yue moved her copies inside. The charcoal stock needed separate inspection where ash had settled on open samples. The worker responsible for the vent did not know the cause yet. Yue recorded the observation and timing without writing that an owner had deliberately poisoned the yard. An event could demand immediate action before its full cause was understood.

wintercity_e03_059.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_059.text: The vent worker found a clogged ordinary screen. Clearing it reduced the escaped ash, and the workshop scheduled a follow-up inspection. The yard cleaned the affected surfaces before resuming the exposed checks. No compensation decision had been made by the time Yue's shift ended. She left that field unresolved. A practical repair and a liability claim could proceed on different schedules, and the people affected should not have to pretend one had completed merely because the other had begun.

wintercity_e03_060.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_060.text: At her lodging, she prepared the next letter to her mother but held it for one more day. She wanted to include the actual end of the arrival interval and her completed wage receipt, rather than make her mother interpret an unfinished account. She wrote the ordinary questions first: whether the shorter tasks still suited the shoulder, whether help at the high shelf remained available, and when a visit might be welcome if travel could be arranged. Her mother would decide what she wanted to disclose.

wintercity_e03_061.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_061.text: Yue checked the travel purse again. Thirty-two copper remained inside it. That amount did not prove she could afford every city plan, and she had no reason to tell her mother that she was rich. It did establish one concrete reserve made from wages already paid. She marked any future support she might send as a separate decision, with a separate source, not a claim on the same coins twice. Money became misleading when the warmth of several intentions concealed that they all used one purse.

wintercity_e03_062.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_062.text: On Day 835, the fuel-yard comparison was routine until the final receipt. A clerk had entered a cylinder serial number with two digits reversed. Yue found the error because the rack sheet and return sheet disagreed, then checked the physical housing. The correction followed the object actually present. Nobody searched for a nonexistent missing cylinder after the number was repaired. Lan thanked her for the comparison, and Yue accepted the thanks without turning a day's accurate work into permission for a larger apparatus role.

wintercity_e03_063.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_063.text: At the shift's end, Yan invited her to observe the next week's low-load rehearsals. Observation would cost an afternoon but no practice fuel. Yue put the date beside the calendar meeting and her continuing limited work hours. She could not attend every useful event in the city. Choosing where to spend time would decide which facts she later knew directly, and which she would have to ask someone else to explain. A calendar was already a record of paths she would not take.

wintercity_e03_064.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e03_064.text: The first service days had made the city's systems less mysterious and its limits more visible. Heat required compatible supplies, return paths, and people willing to do ordinary maintenance. Care required staffed rooms and actual time. Yue's small circuit remained her own tested capacity, neither diminished by being modest nor enlarged by standing near great works. Tomorrow the closure calendar would demand attention. She folded the week's stock sheets, leaving every spent quantity spent and every unresolved question available to be answered.

wintercity_arrival_open_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_open_001.text: At the public-source desk, Yue found the worker-authorized failure sheets on the reader's table beside their redaction notice. The reader had identified a possible comparison with the winter city's connector inspections. She wanted the warning's permitted public wording before mentioning the mine. Yue showed the actual release, leaving raw interviews and private worker names absent. She could verify the copied phrase from the authorized source. She could not supply a private method description merely because the city's question seemed worthwhile.

wintercity_arrival_open_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_open_002.text: They corrected a catalogue line that had called Yue the workers' permanent representative. She held permission for specified public findings, not a continuing mandate over every new request. The reader replaced the line with the named source authorization and kept the correction visible. Yue spent the afternoon checking the public comparison references. That work used no laboratory seat, instrument, or cylinder. Its result was a bounded reference sheet that could later support a public service question without making an unperformed technical trial appear.

wintercity_arrival_open_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_open_003.text: The desk scheduled the final acknowledgement within the remaining arrival interval. Yue retained her permitted duplicate and a copy of today's correction. Open circulation had made a practical city comparison possible, while its privacy limits still protected the unshared testimony.

wintercity_arrival_guarded_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_guarded_001.text: Yue reached the calibrated bench on the afternoon of Day 830. The custodian checked the prepaid six-copper seat receipt, the two-hour window, and the method owners' consent for the retained private comparison copy. Other users still had their own nonexclusive appointments. Yue waited for the preceding user to return the ordinary model to its marked position. The seat payment covered time and custody supervision. No cylinder, mine instrument, or finished circuit fuel stood ready for her merely because the door had opened.

wintercity_arrival_guarded_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_guarded_002.text: She used the appointment for the permitted comparison of uncharged control geometry and the consented private notes. The custodian inspected the ordinary model before and afterward. Yue did not power a task, claim a cultivation advance, or convert a written input into a measured result. A discrepancy in one copied orientation became a question for the method owners through the agreed private channel. Its correction might matter later; today she marked it unresolved rather than silently adjust the original.

wintercity_arrival_guarded_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_guarded_003.text: At the end of two hours, she returned the model and signed the bench closure. The custodian sealed the city-held comparison copy for its scheduled return. The actual afternoon had provided bounded private reference work, not a public seminar or a new factory appointment. Yue left with her own permitted notes and the custody receipt. The finite seat had been used and ended; it could not be spent again at another apparatus.

wintercity_arrival_exit_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_exit_001.text: Yue had no mine-derived appointment on Day 830. After her counting shift, she went to the public information shelf available to ordinary visitors. She could compare the city's published connector description with her own nonconfidential observations, but she had no authorized worker finding or private method copy to add. The resulting questions remained hers. The reader accepted a request for the public inspection summary and declined to label it a mine-delegated comparison. That precise limit saved everybody a misleading attribution.

wintercity_arrival_exit_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_exit_002.text: With the remaining afternoon, Yue checked the public-room route she would need if her lodging's available warmth ended. A roadworker showed her the posted temporary diversion, and she walked it before writing the time. She paid for her own food and returned without borrowing an instrument or a source cover. Declining the mine posts had freed this afternoon for ordinary city preparation, while leaving the private bench and its particular comparison unavailable.

wintercity_arrival_exit_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_arrival_exit_003.text: She filed the public request under her own name. Any later apparatus application would depend on a separate paid booking and the qualifications she actually held. No closed mine duty remained to reopen for convenience.
